title: Descent data on affine morphisms are effective for an fpqc covering $\{X\to S\}$ (Stacks 0245)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] such that the one-member family $\{f:X\to S\}$ is an fpqc covering of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Let $V\to X$ be an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and let $\varphi$ be a descent datum on $V$ over $X/S$ [def-pd-descent-datum]: an isomorphism $\varphi:\mathrm{pr}_0^*V\to\mathrm{pr}_1^*V$ of schemes over $X_2=X\times_SX$ [def-pc-fibre-product], where $\mathrm{pr}_0,\mathrm{pr}_1:X_2\to X$ are the projections, satisfying $\mathrm{pr}_{02}^*\varphi=\mathrm{pr}_{12}^*\varphi\circ\mathrm{pr}_{01}^*\varphi$ over $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Then $(V,\varphi)$ is effective: there are a scheme $U$ with a morphism $U\to S$ and an isomorphism $\psi:U\times_SX\to V$ of schemes over $X$ such that $\varphi\circ\mathrm{pr}_0^*\psi=\mathrm{pr}_1^*\psi\circ\mathrm{can}_U$, where $\mathrm{can}_U:\mathrm{pr}_0^*(U\times_SX)\to\mathrm{pr}_1^*(U\times_SX)$ is the composite of the canonical isomorphisms of both sides with $U\times_SX_2$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (affine morphisms are stable under base change: hypothesis (1) of [lem-galois-fpqc-descending-types-morphisms] for $\mathcal P$ = affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]).* If $Y\to V$ is affine and $V'\to V$ is any morphism of schemes, then $Y\times_VV'\to V'$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (1). (Source: 'Being affine is a property of morphisms of schemes which is ... preserved under any base change, see Morphisms, Lemma 01SD'.)

proof.text: Prove finite coproduct stability directly in Lean: the coprojections form an open cover. Disjointness of their images and Sigma.ι_map identify the pullback of the sum map along the i-th coprojection with the i-th component map. IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.of_openCover and invariance under isomorphism prove the sum map affine. This replaces the clopen-idempotent argument.

Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-descending-types-morphisms] to the affine morphism property. Base change stability is Step 1, finite coproduct stability is Step 2, and the affine flat surjective case is [lem-galois-affine-flat-descent-effective]. The resulting conclusion is effectivity for the given singleton fpqc cover.
